articles.title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
articles.description: Sales of essential goods such as hand sanitiser soar after the government called on households to be prepared for emergencies.
articles.summary: Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.
key_points: Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.
The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.
However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.

articles.description: AI safety regulator will also be created after a rogue OpenAI agent hacked government websites.
articles.summary: PM Anthony Albanese says the law needs to catch up with a "fast-changing world" Australia plans to create a new AI safety regulator and has flagged criminal penalties for tech companies who do not comply, months after an OpenAI hack.
key_points: In September, Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese revealed that a rogue OpenAI agent had "infiltrated" a government health website and other systems, and criticised the company for taking months to tell them about…
On Tuesday, he released the 18 recommendations made after a "rapid review" into the breaches including new safety and security standards for AI companies such as mandatory reporting of hacks.
AI brings opportunities, he said, but Australia must prepare for the "new risks" from this "rapidly advancing technology".
